evidence_records.statement: A higher proportion of renter households spending 35 percent or more of income on rent indicates substantial housing cost burden.
evidence_records.relevance: High housing costs can contribute to financial instability and reduce resources available for healthcare.

evidence_records.statement: Higher SNAP household concentration indicates greater community-level economic vulnerability.
evidence_records.relevance: Economic instability can create barriers to maintaining healthcare access and meeting basic needs.

evidence_records.statement: A higher proportion of households with moderate overcrowding indicates increased housing pressure.
evidence_records.relevance: Crowded housing conditions can affect health, privacy, stress, and exposure to illness.

evidence_records.statement: Households without vehicles located beyond accessible straight-line distances may face transportation barriers.
evidence_records.relevance: Transportation limitations may interfere with healthcare access and continuity of care.

evidence_records.statement: Routine checkup prevalence provides an indicator of preventive healthcare utilization.
evidence_records.relevance: Lower preventive-care utilization may indicate barriers to routine healthcare engagement.

evidence_records.statement: Higher obesity prevalence indicates greater community-level metabolic health burden.
evidence_records.relevance: Elevated obesity prevalence can indicate increased need for community wellness and prevention resources.

evidence_records.statement: A higher proportion of adults with less than a ninth-grade education indicates lower educational attainment.
evidence_records.relevance: Lower educational attainment may create barriers to health literacy, healthcare navigation, and understanding health information.

evidence_records.statement: A higher number of low-income, low-access census tracts indicates increased geographic transportation vulnerability.
evidence_records.relevance: Low-access areas may experience reduced ability to reach healthcare and essential services.

evidence_records.statement: Higher physical inactivity prevalence indicates greater community-level inactivity burden.
evidence_records.relevance: Physical inactivity may contribute to chronic disease risk and indicates potential need for wellness resources.

evidence_records.statement: Higher COPD prevalence indicates greater community-level respiratory disease burden.
evidence_records.relevance: Respiratory disease burden may increase the need for chronic disease and community health support.

evidence_records.statement: Cholesterol screening prevalence provides an indicator of preventive healthcare engagement.
evidence_records.relevance: Lower screening utilization may indicate barriers to preventive healthcare access.

evidence_records.statement: Households without vehicles located beyond accessible driving distances may face increased transportation barriers.
evidence_records.relevance: Limited transportation options can make healthcare access and appointment attendance more difficult.

evidence_records.statement: Higher diabetes prevalence indicates greater community-level chronic disease burden.
evidence_records.relevance: Elevated chronic disease burden may indicate increased need for prevention and community health resources.

evidence_records.statement: A higher proportion of severely overcrowded households indicates significant housing pressure.
evidence_records.relevance: Severe overcrowding may increase health risks and indicate housing instability.

evidence_records.statement: A higher low-access population indicates greater geographic transportation barriers to essential services.
evidence_records.relevance: Transportation barriers may reduce access to healthcare and other essential community resources.

evidence_records.statement: A higher proportion of renter households spending 30 to 34.9 percent of income on rent indicates increased housing cost burden.
evidence_records.relevance: Housing cost burden can reduce resources available for healthcare, transportation, food, and other basic needs.

evidence_records.statement: Higher prevalence of poor physical health indicates greater community-level physical health burden.
evidence_records.relevance: Poor physical health burden may indicate increased need for healthcare navigation and community support.
